summary: Chapter 2 stages Feuz's archive investigation converging on Stettler at the Pfarrhaus, but as written it renames the victim, invents an autopsy and a poisoning to replace the canonical fall, changes Stettler's office, relocates Berta into domestic service for another man, and lets Rutz read as two unlinked people, so it does not earn its place against canon.

issues.fix_hint: Rename her Klara Vogel, per the name registry; cut the invented first name 'Anna' and the invented maiden name 'geborene Aebi'.
Cut the Sektionsbefund for Melchior's file; canon states no autopsy was performed and the certificate was filed on the fall alone.

issues.unit: die Zusammensetzung des Präparats, das man im Magen gefunden hatte
issues.fix_hint: Replace the poison-composition detail with canon's reused certificate phrase 'Herzversagen, vermutlich beim Sturz', identical across both files.
Replace 'Amtsstatthalter' with 'Amtsarzt' throughout (both occurrences); canon gives Stettler's office as district physician, not district administrator.

issues.unit: schöpfte den Kaffee ein... stellte die Tasse vor ihn hin
issues.fix_hint: Cut the domestic-service framing; canon makes Berta the widow of Melchior, not a housekeeper serving Feuz (or any other man) in his home.

issues.unit: der Pfarrer stand in der Tür
issues.fix_hint: Name him Rutz (or Pfarrer Rutz) at least once in this scene so the priest at the Pfarrhaus is unambiguously the same person as the creditor Rutz introduced earlier, not a second, unnamed character.

issues.unit: Feuz hatte in zwanzig Jahren keinen
issues.fix_hint: Soften or cut 'in zwanzig Jahren' of tenure; canon describes Feuz as young, which sits oddly with two decades of career observation.
